thread.title: Apple beats on earnings, but stock falls after December outlook misses - MarketWatch

author: Emily Bary
title: Apple beats on earnings, but stock falls after December outlook misses - MarketWatch
text:
Apple Inc. reported better-than-expected financial results for its fiscal fourth quarter, but shares sank in after-hours trading Thursday after the company delivered a disappointing forecast for the holiday period.
The trillion-dollar company delivered earnings per share of $2.91 on revenue of $62.9 billion for its latest quarter, ahead of the FactSet consensus expectation of $2.78 in EPS and $61.5 billion in revenue. Apple’s AAPL, +1.54% iPhone revenue positively surprised as well, coming in at $37.2 billion for the quarter, whereas analysts had been calling for $35.6 billion. The average selling price for an iPhone during the quarter was $793, far above the $751 projection.

See Also How to Stop Iran Oil-Sanction Busters? Take 50 Million Photos a Day × The smartphone manufacturer’s December-quarter forecast , however, fell short of expectations. Apple projects sales for the holiday quarter of $89 billion to $93 billion, whereas analysts had been called for revenue of $92.9 billion. Ahead of the report, Morgan Stanley analyst Katy Huberty called Apple’s December-quarter outlook “the most important driver of investor sentiment.”
Shares were last down more than 4% after hours.
Apple’s China business, an area of concern going into the report, showed momentum in the September period. Apple reported $11.4 billion in Greater China revenue for the quarter, up from $9.8 billion a year earlier. Investors had been worried that trade-war tensions, macroeconomic issues and a freeze on new game approvals in China might impact consumer spending in the region.
The company fell short of expectations with its services business, which logged $9.98 billion in revenue compared with the $10.2 billion that analysts had been expecting. The services business includes the App Store, Apple Music and other fast-growing areas of Apple’s business. Services revenue grew 17% in the quarter, while iPhone revenue climbed 29% and “other products” revenue increased by 31%. The “other products” segment includes the Apple Watch and AirPods.
Apple shares have gained 33.2% over the past 12 months, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +1.06% has gained 8.3%.
